record.paper_title: Towards Event-Triggered NMPC for Efficient 6G Communications: Experimental Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Stability under retransmissions and correlated latency peaks
record.original_question: How can a sensor-side event-triggered nonlinear model predictive controller over a 5G or future-6G wireless network maintain stability when poor channel conditions cause significant packet errors, Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request retransmissions, variable uplink and downlink delays, and multiple correlated latency peaks? The controller must handle the fact that uplink retransmission delays can be measured and included in delay compensation, whereas downlink retransmission delays are not correctly compensated when downlink delay is assumed constant; experiments showed stability with some latency peaks above 100 ms but failure when several correlated peaks occurred.

evidence.quote: However, at −10 dB, increased channel interference leads to significant packet errors. If the receiver of a message cannot decode the packet, it sends a negative-acknowledgment to the transmitter of the message, which performs an HARQ retransmission.

From a control perspective, if such an HARQ retransmission occurs in the uplink direction, i.e., from the plant to the controller, the uplink delay increases and will be measured and accounted for by the delay compensation. Meanwhile, if the packet error occurs in the downlink direction from the controller to the actuator, the increased downlink delay is not being correctly compensated by the delay compensation, since the downlink delay is assumed constant.

Despite this, the system maintains stability even with latency peaks exceeding 100 ms. However, when multiple correlated latency peaks occur at around t=8 s, the controller fails to maintain stability, causing the pendulum arm to fall and leading to an increased closed-loop cost.
While the networked control system is robust to delays up to 100 ms, prolonged delays due to poor channel conditions can affect the stability of the control application.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a networked control system in which a nonlinear plant with state $x(t)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and input $u(t)\in\mathbb{R}^m$ evolves according to $\dot{x}(t) = f(x(t), u(t))$, with $f$ Lipschitz and $f(0,0)=0$. A sensor co-located with the plant samples $x$ and runs an event-triggered nonlinear model predictive controller (NMPC): at each sampling instant $t_k$ the sensor decides whether to transmit $x(t_k)$ over a wireless uplink to a remote controller; whenever a transmission occurs, the controller solves a finite-horizon optimal control problem and sends an input trajectory over a wireless downlink to an actuator that applies it in open loop until the next update.

The wireless channel introduces:
(i) a stochastic uplink delay $	au^{\mathrm{up}}_k \ge 0$ that can be time-stamped and measured at the controller, so it can be exactly compensated for in the prediction;
(ii) a stochastic downlink delay $	au^{\mathrm{dn}}_k \ge 0$ that is treated by the controller as a fixed constant $ ar	au^{\mathrm{dn}}$, so any deviation $	au^{\mathrm{dn}}_k -  ar	au^{\mathrm{dn}}$ is an uncompensated mismatch;
(iii) packet errors triggering Hybrid ARQ retransmissions, which can produce correlated bursts of latency peaks (delays exceeding a nominal threshold such as $100$ ms) on consecutive samples in either direction.

Let $\{	au^{\mathrm{up}}_k, 	au^{\mathrm{dn}}_k, e_k\}$ be a stochastic process where $e_k\in\{0,1\}$ indicates a packet error at step $k$, with possibly strong temporal correlation (latency-peak clustering).

Problem. Design an event-triggering rule, a delay-compensation/prediction scheme, and an NMPC formulation (including terminal ingredients and a robustness margin against the uncompensated downlink delay variation) such that the resulting closed-loop system is input-to-state stable (or stable in an appropriate stochastic sense, e.g., almost-sure boundedness or mean-square stability) under bursts of correlated latency peaks and HARQ retransmissions in both directions, and provide explicit, verifiable sufficient conditions on the channel statistics (peak magnitude, burst length, correlation structure) and on the NMPC parameters (horizon, sampling period, terminal set, triggering threshold) under which stability is guaranteed.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem concerning stability of event-triggered NMPC over 5G/6G wireless links under HARQ retransmissions and correlated latency bursts. While there is a substantial literature on NMPC robustness to bounded random delays and packet losses, no general result is currently known that gives verifiable stability conditions under correlated burst delays with asymmetrically (un)compensated uplink/downlink delays as described. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Towards Event-Triggered NMPC for Efficient 6G Communications
status_evidence.snippet: Stability is preserved with some latency peaks above 100 ms but lost under correlated peaks; downlink delay is not properly compensated.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of guaranteeing stability under correlated latency peaks and HARQ-induced delays is explicitly stated as an open issue.
